newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria faults Libyan leader on Arab unity plans.
newsitem.headline: Algeria faults Libyan leader on Arab unity plans.

text.p: Algeria, through its official news agency APS, accused Libyan leader Muammar Gaddafi of an approach to Arab unity that undermines regional stability.

"The Libyan leader, by declaring casually he no longer recognises the border between Algeria and Libya, does not serve at all the objective of union...and is part of a logic laden with danger for stability of the region's countries," said APS in a Monday commentary seen as reflecting the government view.

The agency said Algeria's borders had been drawn with "the blood of its martyrs" and unity could only be achieved gradually by economic, cultural and political achievements, not by a decision to abolish borders.
APS also rebuffed Gaddafi's statement that Algeria is experiencing a civil war: "This is a way to dodge condemning those who are responsible for the suffering of the Algerian people."

The Algerian government has been battling Moslem guerrillas since 1992 when the authorities cancelled a general election in which radical Islamists had taken a huge lead. About 60,000 people have died.
Gaddafi called last weekend on Libyans to start marchs this year on Egypt, Tunisia, Sudan and Algeria to impose a merger: "The Pan-Arab Unity will be implemented by the start of the 21th century."
